claim: Larval Drosophila has approximately 10,000 neurons in its brain
source: The Drosophila larva is a favorable model system for the study of learning and memory formation (Gerber et al., 2013; Widmann et al., 2018; Quinn and Dudai, 1976; Scherer et al., 2003; Apostolopoulou et al., 2013; Neuser et al., 2005; Saumweber et al., 2018), with approximately 10,000 neurons in its representative insect brain.
evidence: The manuscript directly states the number of neurons in the larval Drosophila brain, supported by citations to previous work

claim: Larvae avoid carbon dioxide (CO2) at all concentrations
source: Drosophila larvae avoid carbon dioxide (CO2) at all concentrations (Faucher et al., 2006; Jones et al., 2007; Kwon et al., 2007; Gershow et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by multiple citations to previous studies

claim: At 18% CO2 concentration, larvae with functional CO2 receptors chose the CO2-containing channel about 25% of the time
source: At the 18% concentration used throughout this work, larvae with functional CO2 receptors chose the CO2-containing channel about 25% of the time.
evidence: This is a direct statement of experimental results from the study

claim: Gr63a1 larvae lacking a functional CO2 receptor were indifferent to the presence of CO2
source: Gr63a1 (Jones et al., 2007) larvae lacking a functional CO2 receptor were indifferent to the presence of CO2 in the channel (Figure 1B)
evidence: The claim is stated in text and supported by data shown in Figure 1B

claim: Activation of the DAN-i1 pair of mushroom body input neurons acts as a reward for associative learning
source: Activation of the DAN-i1 pair of mushroom body input neurons has been shown to act as a reward for associative learning (Saumweber et al., 2018; Thum and Gerber, 2019; Schleyer et al., 2020; Weiglein et al., 2019; Eschbach et al., 2020b).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by multiple citations

claim: Pairing DAN-i1 activation with CO2 presentation causes larvae to become indifferent to CO2 following 20 training cycles
source: We found that in the paired group, larvae became indifferent to CO2 presentation following 20 training cycles (Figure 1D, DANi1>CsChrimson, Paired).
evidence: This is a direct statement of experimental results shown in Figure 1D

claim: Reverse-paired training (DAN-i1 activated when only air was present) did not cause a change in CO2 preference
source: We did not observe any change in preference in the reverse-paired group (DANi1>CsChrimson, Reverse-Paired).
evidence: This is a direct statement of experimental results

claim: Larvae not fed all-trans-retinal (ATR) did not show a preference change following paired training
source: Nor did we observe a preference change following paired training for genetically identical animals not fed all-trans-retinal (ATR), a necessary co-factor for CsChrimson function (DANi1>CsChrimson, Paired ATR-).
evidence: This is a direct statement of experimental results serving as a control

claim: Learning requires CO2 to predict the reward, not just coincidence between CO2 and reward
source: In fact, we only found an increase in CO2 preference following training in which the CO2 predicted the reward (Figure 1D).
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from experimental data comparing different temporal relationships between CO2 and reward

claim: Reward prediction is both necessary and sufficient for learning in this assay
source: We found an increased CO2 preference for animals in this first group only (Figure 1E), indicating that reward prediction is both necessary and sufficient for learning in this assay.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from experimental data testing different temporal relationships

claim: Learning is quantized and all-or-none rather than graded
source: We found that the data were better described by the quantized learning model (Table 4): larvae form two discrete groups, with the fraction in the trained group increasing with each cycle of additional training.
evidence: This conclusion is based on model fitting to experimental data

claim: The fraction of untrained larvae exponentially decreases with increasing training
source: We plotted the fraction of untrained larvae vs. number of training cycles and saw that the fraction of larvae in the untrained group exponentially decreased with increasing training (Figure 2E, note logarithmic y-axis on insert).
evidence: This is a direct statement of results shown in Figure 2E

claim: The all-or-none quantized model best describes the learning data according to BIC and AIC criteria
source: According to standard selection rules (BIC and AIC), the all-or-none quantized model best describes the data (Table 4).
evidence: This conclusion is based on statistical model comparison

claim: Unrewarded CO2 presentations following training reversed the effect of training
source: In contrast, unrewarded CO2 presentations following training reversed the effect of training; for small (2 or 3 cycles) amounts of training, the reversal was almost complete (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is a direct statement of experimental results on extinction

claim: Unrewarded CO2 presentation prior to training had no effect on the eventual preference change
source: When we compared the 'habituated' groups of larvae to larvae trained for the same number of cycles without habituation or extinction, we found that unrewarded CO2 presentation prior to training had no effect on the eventual preference change (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is a direct statement of experimental results

claim: Larvae subject to training then extinction reverted to their 'untrained' state rather than an intermediate state
source: In all cases, we observed two groups with the same central means and no evidence of a third intermediate group. We concluded that larvae subject to training then extinction reverted to their 'untrained' state.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from analysis of preference distributions

claim: Larvae can still learn if they receive additional training directly following extinction
source: We found that following this training-extinction-training protocol, both the population preference for CO2 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B) and the fraction of larvae trained (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C) were comparable to larvae that had been trained three times without extinction cycles.
evidence: This is a direct statement of experimental results

claim: Following 20 cycles of training, larvae became indifferent to CO2 and this indifference persisted to the next day
source: We found that following 20 cycles of training, larvae became indifferent to CO2 and this indifference persisted to the next day.
evidence: This is a direct statement of experimental results on overnight memory retention

claim: Most larvae switched preference following five cycles of training and retained that preference overnight
source: Similarly, we found that most larvae switched preference following five cycles of training and retained that preference overnight.
evidence: This is a direct statement of experimental results

claim: Two cycles of training were sufficient to form a memory lasting overnight when larvae were not tested immediately after training
source: When we tested these larvae the next day, we found that they showed decreased avoidance of CO2. This indicated that two cycles of training were sufficient to form a memory lasting overnight, but that immediate exposure to unrewarded CO2 following this short training interval likely reversed the effects of training
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from experimental results comparing different protocols

claim: Overnight consolidation made memories more resistant to extinction
source: The only difference between the two experiments was whether we attempted extinction immediately after training or the next day. Thus, we concluded that overnight consolidation made memories more resistant to extinction.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from comparing extinction effects at different time points

claim: Massed training (20 cycles) produced cycloheximide-resistant memory
source: We found that performances tested immediately and 16 hr after training were both unaffected by CXM treatment. Following 20 cycles of training, larvae from both groups (ATR+/CXM+; ATR+/CXM-) became indifferent to CO2 and this indifference persisted to the next day (Figure 4C). This suggests that the memory formation was independent of de novo protein synthesis.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from experimental results with cycloheximide treatment

claim: Spaced training produced cycloheximide-sensitive memory (LTM)
source: We found that 1 day following spaced training, ATR+/CXM+ larvae continued to avoid CO2, while ATR+/CXM- larvae did not. This indicated that spaced training formed a memory whose retention was disrupted by CXM.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from experimental results with cycloheximide treatment and spaced training

claim: Massed training produces anesthesia-resistant memory (ARM) while spaced training produces long-term memory (LTM)
source: Thus, we identified spaced training as producing long-term memory (LTM) and the massed training as producing anesthesia-resistant memory (ARM).
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the differential effects of cycloheximide on massed vs. spaced training

claim: Heat-shock induced dCREB2-b expression disrupted memory retention following spaced but not massed training
source: We found that, congruent with our CXM experiments, the day after spaced training, heat-shocked larvae (Figure 4D,S 10x, HS) avoided CO2 to the same extent they did prior to training, while larvae that were not heat-shocked (Figure 4D,S 10X, No HS) retained learned indifference; larvae that received massed training (Figure 4D,M 10x, HS and No HS) retained their learned indifference overnight, regardless of heat-shock.
evidence: This is a direct statement of experimental results using heat-shock inducible CREB repressor

claim: The Y-maze assay allows for repeated measurements of individual larva's olfactory preferences
source: Establishing the degree to which an individual larva seeks out or avoids an odorant requires repeated measurements of that larva's response to the odor. We developed a Y-maze assay (Buchanan et al., 2015; Werkhoven et al., 2019) to repeatedly test an individual's olfactory preference.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the capabilities of the new assay

claim: The Y-maze assay allows for in situ training without handling animals between training and testing
source: Compared to the existing paradigm, our assay allows for measuring individual animals' changes in preference due to training, allows for greater control of the temporal relation between the conditioned and unconditioned stimuli, and does not require any handling of the animals between training and testing.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the advantages of the new assay

claim: Silencing the Mushroom Body did not impair innate CO2 avoidance
source: Silencing the Mushroom Body (OK107>Kir2.1) did not impair innate CO2 avoidance.
evidence: This is a direct statement of experimental results

claim: Animals in which CO2 receptor neurons were silenced were indifferent to CO2 presence
source: as were animals in which the CO2 receptor neurons were silenced (Gr21a>Kir.21), indicating that larvae responded to the presence of CO2 and not some other property of the CO2 containing air stream.
evidence: This is a direct statement of experimental results serving as a control

claim: Decreasing CO2 concentration decreased innate avoidance of CO2
source: We presented lower concentrations of CO2 both during the training and testing phases, and found that decreasing the CO2 concentration decreased innate avoidance of CO2.
evidence: This is a direct statement of experimental results

claim: No larvae showed statistically significant attraction to CO2 at any concentration tested after training
source: In all cases, following training, larvae lost avoidance to CO2 but none showed statistically significant attraction (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is a direct statement of experimental results

claim: Activation of 58E02-labeled neurons (DAN-i1, DAN-h1, DAN-j1) did not produce stronger learning than DAN-i1 activation alone
source: We repeated the training protocol, substituting 58E02 activation for DAN-i1 activation alone, but did not see an increased preference following training compared to DAN-i1 activation alone (Figure 1D, 58E02>CsChrimson).
evidence: This is a direct statement of experimental results

claim: Larvae are sensitive to both the timing and context of reward presentation
source: Using this device, we find that larvae are sensitive to both the timing and context of the reward presentation
evidence: This is a summary conclusion drawn from multiple experiments

claim: These results are the first demonstrations that larvae can retain memories overnight
source: These results are the first demonstrations that larvae can retain memories overnight
evidence: This is a direct claim about the novelty of the findings

claim: Larvae trained in the assay retained memories for 16-20 hours
source: We found that larvae trained in our assay retained memories overnight: 16–20 hr.
evidence: This is a direct statement of experimental results

claim: Larvae have been shown to retain odor-electric shock memories for at least 8 hours
source: Larvae trained to associate odor with electric shock form memories that persist for at least 8 hr (Khurana et al., 2009).
evidence: This is a statement about previous work, supported by citation

claim: Odor-salt memories have been shown to partially persist for at least 5 hours
source: Odor-salt memories have been shown to partially persist for at least 5 hr (Widmann et al., 2016; Eschment et al., 2020)
evidence: This is a statement about previous work, supported by citations

claim: Odor-salt memories can be protein-synthesis dependent, depending on the initial feeding state of the larva
source: and can be protein-synthesis dependent (Eschment et al., 2020), depending on the initial feeding state of the larva.
evidence: This is a statement about previous work, supported by citation

claim: Overnight memory retention has not been previously demonstrated in the larva
source: Overnight memory retention, whether or not requiring protein-synthesis, has not been demonstrated in the larva
evidence: This is a statement about the state of the field prior to this work

claim: Long-lasting retention of appetitive memories has not been previously demonstrated in larvae
source: nor has long-lasting retention of appetitive memories.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of the field prior to this work

claim: The Y-mazes are constructed from agarose with channels slightly larger than the larvae
source: The Y-mazes (Figure 1A) are constructed from agarose with channels slightly larger than the larvae, allowing free crawling only in a straight line (Heckscher et al., 2012; Sun and Heckscher, 2016).
evidence: This is a direct description of the experimental apparatus

claim: Custom computer vision software detects the motion of the larva in real time
source: Custom computer vision software detects the motion of the larva while computer controlled valves manipulate the direction of airflow so that the larva is always presented with a fresh set of choices each time it approaches the intersection (Figure 1A, Figure 1—video 1).
evidence: This is a direct description of the experimental apparatus and methods

claim: The probability of choosing CO2 increased as CO2 concentration decreased
source: The probability of choosing the CO2 containing channel increased as CO2 concentration in that channel decreased (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is a direct statement of experimental results

claim: Pigeons, rats, and rabbits have all been shown to experience sudden performance increases in learning tasks
source: Pigeons, rats, and rabbits have all been shown to experience sudden performance increases in learning tasks, suggesting quantized learning may be a generalized phenomenon (Gallistel et al., 2004).
evidence: This is a statement about previous work in other species, supported by citation

claim: There was no evidence of a cumulative effect of prior training in the probability that a given cycle would induce a state transition
source: We found no evidence of a cumulative effect of prior training in the probability that a given cycle of training would induce a state transition in larvae that had not already transitioned.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from analysis of the learning data

claim: Repeated cycles of training stabilized memories against later extinction
source: We did, however, find evidence that repeated cycles of training stabilized memories against later extinction effected by presentation of CO2 without reward.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from extinction experiments

claim: The results are entirely congruent with observations in adult flies regarding ARM and LTM
source: These results are the first demonstrations that larvae can retain memories overnight; they are entirely congruent with observations in adult flies.
evidence: This is a comparison of the current results to previous work in adults

claim: In adult Drosophila, whether ARM or LTM is formed depends on the training protocol
source: In adult Drosophila, whether ARM or LTM is formed depends on the training protocol (Tully et al., 1990; Tully et al., 1994; Yin et al., 1995; Yu et al., 2006; Bouzaiane et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a statement about previous work in adult flies, supported by citations

claim: Massed training in adults results in ARM while spaced training produces LTM
source: 'Massed' training, in which all conditioning occurs in rapid sequence without rest intervals, results in ARM, while 'spaced' training, in which the conditioning occurs in blocks separated by intervals of time, produces LTM.
evidence: This is a statement about previous work in adult flies

claim: 95% of ATR+/CXM- larvae pupated while only 45% of ATR+/CXM+ larvae pupated
source: To further verify CXM ingestion, we placed ATR+/CXM+ and ATR+/CXM- larvae on clean food and allowed them to continue development. 95% of ATR+/CXM- larvae pupated, while only 45% of ATR+/CXM+ larvae pupated.
evidence: This is a direct statement of experimental results verifying cycloheximide ingestion

claim: Immediately following spaced training, heat-shocked larvae continued to avoid CO2, showing that memory formation was impaired on a relatively short timescale
source: Immediately following spaced training (80 min after the initiation of the spaced training protocol), heat-shocked larvae continued to avoid CO2, showing that memory formation was impaired on a relatively short timescale.
evidence: This is a direct statement of experimental results

claim: The conditioned stimulus (CO2) is sensed by a single pair of genetically identified sensory neurons
source: The conditioned stimulus is sensed by a single pair of genetically identified sensory neurons
evidence: This is a statement about the neural circuit underlying the behavior

claim: The unconditioned stimulus is provided by activation of a single pair of genetically identified reward neurons whose connectivity has been fully reconstructed
source: the unconditioned stimulus is provided by activation of a single pair of genetically identified reward neurons whose connectivity has been fully reconstructed (Schleyer et al., 2020).
evidence: This is a statement about the neural circuit, supported by citation

claim: Existing behavioral assays for larval learning and memory do not address individual animals
source: but existing behavioral assays for larval learning and memory do not address individual animals
evidence: This is a statement about limitations of previous methods

claim: It has been difficult to form long-lasting memories in larvae, especially those requiring synaptic reorganization
source: and it has been difficult to form long-lasting memories, especially those requiring synaptic reorganization.
evidence: This is a statement about limitations of previous work

claim: When coupled to CO2 presentation in appropriate temporal sequence, optogenetic reward reduces avoidance of CO2
source: We confirm that when coupled to CO2 presentation in appropriate temporal sequence, optogenetic reward reduces avoidance of CO2.
evidence: This is a summary statement of the main findings

claim: Memories can be extinguished by repeated unrewarded exposure to CO2
source: Memories can be extinguished by repeated unrewarded exposure to CO2
evidence: This is a summary statement of the main findings

claim: Memories are stabilized against extinction by repeated training or overnight consolidation
source: but are stabilized against extinction by repeated training or overnight consolidation.
evidence: This is a summary statement of the main findings

claim: The work demonstrates long-lasting protein synthesis dependent and independent memory formation
source: Finally, we demonstrate long-lasting protein synthesis dependent and independent memory formation.
evidence: This is a summary statement of the main findings

claim: The larval Drosophila brain has synaptic connectivities that can be reconstructed via electron microscopy
source: whose synaptic connectivities can be reconstructed via electron microscopy (Eichler et al., 2017; Eschbach et al., 2020a; Eschbach et al., 2020b).
evidence: This is a statement about available tools, supported by citations

claim: New methods allow direct measurement of neural activity in behaving larvae
source: New methods allow direct measurement of neural activity in behaving larvae (Karagyozov et al., 2018; He et al., 2019; Vaadia et al., 2019)
evidence: This is a statement about available tools, supported by citations

claim: A device has been developed for assaying individual adult flies' innate and learned olfactory preferences
source: Recently, a device has been developed for assaying individual adult flies' innate (Honegger et al., 2020) and learned (Smith et al., 2021) olfactory preferences
evidence: This is a statement about previous work in adults, supported by citations

claim: No comparable assay to the adult individual preference assay exists for the larval stage
source: but no comparable assay exists for the larval stage.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of the field prior to this work

claim: LTM and ARM are consolidated forms of memory controlled by partially separate molecular and anatomical pathways
source: LTM and ARM are consolidated forms of memory controlled by partially separate molecular and anatomical pathways (Isabel et al., 2004; Jacob and Waddell, 2020; Wu et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a statement about established knowledge, supported by citations

claim: ARM is resistant to anesthetic agents
source: ARM is resistant to anesthetic agents (Quinn et al., 1974)
evidence: This is a statement about established knowledge, supported by citation

claim: LTM requires CREB-dependent transcription and de-novo protein synthesis while ARM does not
source: LTM requires cAMP response element-binding protein (CREB)-dependent transcription and de-novo protein synthesis, while ARM does not (Yin et al., 1995; Perazzona et al., 2004).
evidence: This is a statement about established knowledge, supported by citations

claim: Adult flies have been shown to retain memories for up to a week
source: Adults have been shown to retain memories for up to a week (Yin et al., 1995).
evidence: This is a statement about previous work in adults, supported by citation

claim: In the evolving model of learning in Drosophila, different MBONs promote approach or avoidance
source: In this model, different Mushroom Body Output Neurons (MBONs) promote approach or avoidance (Aso et al., 2014; Eschbach and Zlatic, 2020; Perisse et al., 2013; Owald et al., 2015; Owald and Waddell, 2015; Hige et al., 2015)
evidence: This is a statement about the current model of learning, supported by citations

claim: MBONs synapse onto a convergence neuron that integrates their activities
source: and synapse onto a convergence neuron that integrates their activities (Eschbach and Zlatic, 2020).
evidence: This is a statement about the current model, supported by citation

claim: Prior to learning, aversive and appetitive MBONs receive similar drives from Kenyon Cells that respond to specific olfactory signals
source: Prior to learning, aversive and appetitive MBONs are thought to receive similar drives from Kenyon Cells (KCs) that respond to specific olfactory signals.
evidence: This is a statement about the current model of learning

claim: Appetitive learning weakens the connection between KCs encoding a stimulus and avoidance MBONs
source: learning that a stimulus is appetitive weakens the connection between KCs encoding that stimulus and the avoidance MBONs, promoting approach
evidence: This is a statement about the current model, supported by citations in the surrounding text

claim: Aversive conditioning weakens the connection between KCs and approach MBONs
source: while aversive conditioning weakens the connection between KCs and approach MBONs, promoting avoidance (Aso et al., 2014; Owald and Waddell, 2015; Eschbach and Zlatic, 2020).
evidence: This is a statement about the current model, supported by citations

claim: Presentation of CO2 coincident with or prior to DAN-i1 activation likely reduces the ability of CO2 to excite aversive MBONs including MBON-i1
source: According to this model, presentation of CO2 coincident with or prior to the activation of DAN-i1 reduces the ability of CO2 to excite one or more aversive MBONs, likely including MBON-i1, which encodes avoidance (Eschbach and Zlatic, 2020) and is postsynaptic to DAN-i1 (Eichler et al., 2017).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the results in the context of the current model, supported by citations

claim: The learned appetitive drive appears to exactly cancel but not overcome the innate aversion pathway
source: This results in an appetitive drive from the MB that cancels out the innate avoidance pathway. Why in our experiments the learned appetitive drive appears to exactly cancel but not overcome the innate aversion should be the subject of further study
evidence: This is an observation about the results that requires further investigation

claim: Animals are found in only two behavioral states: innate avoidance or learned indifference
source: Animals are found in only two behavioral states: innate avoidance or learned indifference; this likely reflects two discrete states of the underlying neural circuit.
evidence: This is a summary of the findings with an interpretation about neural states

claim: The assay demonstrates long-term protein synthesis dependent memory, implying that memories are encoded in synaptic change
source: We demonstrate long-term protein synthesis dependent memory, implying that memories are encoded in synaptic change.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental results

claim: How larvae navigate in response to CO2 presentation has been described in detail
source: How the larva navigates in response to CO2 presentation has been described in detail (Faucher et al., 2006; Gershow et al., 2012; Gepner et al., 2015; Gepner et al., 2018)
evidence: This is a statement about previous work, supported by citations

claim: How neurons downstream of DAN-i1 and KCs contribute to navigational decision making has been described
source: as has how neurons downstream of DAN-i1 and the KCs contribute to navigational decision making (Eichler et al., 2017; Saumweber et al., 2018; Thum and Gerber, 2019; Schleyer et al., 2020).
evidence: This is a statement about previous work, supported by citations

claim: Out of 443 larvae placed on agar plates to be tested the following day, 439 larvae were recovered and retested
source: Out of 443 larvae placed on agar plates to be tested the following day, 439 larvae were recovered and retested. The four lost larvae were excluded from analysis.
evidence: This is a direct statement about experimental procedures and data handling

claim: After choosing a CO2 containing channel, both naive and trained larvae are less likely to choose the CO2 containing channel the next time they approach the intersection
source: In fact, we found that after choosing a CO2 containing channel, both naive and trained larvae are less likely to choose the CO2 containing channel the next time they approach the intersection.
evidence: This is a direct statement of an observed pattern in the data

claim: The choices made by larvae are not independent
source: Because the choices are not independent, the variance of the mean of a series of choices is not given by Equation 7.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the observed correlation between successive choices
